summary: Beyang Liu (CTO/co-founder of Sourcegraph) and Bruno Passos (Group Product Manager at Booking.com) discuss their partnership building AI agents that deliver real ROI in the enterprise SDLC. Sourcegraph's mission is making software development at scale tractable, offering code search, large-scale refactoring tools, and Cody, an AI coding assistant optimized for large messy codebases. Booking.com is one of the largest online travel agencies, serving 1.5M room nights with 3,000+ developers, 250+ merge requests per year, and 2.5M CI jobs annually. Decades of A/B testing and feature flags bloated the codebase, pushing developer toil above 90%. Their adoption journey started in January with Cody deployed company-wide, initially limited to one LLM. Sourcegraph quickly enabled multi-LLM access, critical because different LLMs excelled at different tasks. Developer training in July proved pivotal—users who initially saw no value became daily active users. By October, they moved beyond unreliable 'time saved' metrics to define four KPIs: lead time for change, quality, coding sites, and codebase modernization. By November, daily Cody users were 30%+ faster and shipped 30% more merge requests, with notably lighter MRs. Engineers began composing Cody API calls into longer chain automations—proto-agents. This led to a joint weeklong hackathon in Amsterdam producing three production agents. The first searches Booking.com's 1M+ token GraphQL schema, agenticly finding relevant nodes and walking up the tree to pull parent nodes, producing far better results than naive approaches. The second targets automated code migration of legacy functions with 10,000+ lines, using code search, structured meta-prompts, and divide-and-conquer—within two days of the hackathon, they identified call sites that had taken developers months to map previously. The third is a customizable code review agent where organizations define rules in a flat file format and the agent applies relevant rules to modified files in PRs, optimizing precision over recall. Looking ahead, Bruno envisions declaring service rules, shifting CI errors left into the IDE with suggested fixes, and enabling self-healing services. Beyang connects this to the Mythical Man Month problem—successful software accumulates tech debt and loses cohesion—and sees declarative rule enforcement as a way for senior engineers to maintain standards at scale. Both speakers emphasize education as the single most important takeaway: handholding entire business units through two-day workshops and hackathons transformed skeptics into passionate daily users.

sections.title: Introduction and Context
sections.summary: Beyang Liu (Sourcegraph CTO/co-founder) and Bruno Passos (Booking.com, Developer Experience and GenAI lead) introduce themselves and the topic: building software development agents with real ROI. Beyang frames the common scenario where CEOs demand AI adoption and CFOs later ask for measurable ROI.

sections.title: Booking.com Scale and Codebase Bloat Problem
sections.summary: Bruno describes Booking.com as one of the largest online travel agencies serving 1.5M room nights with 3,000+ developers, 250+ merge requests/year, and 2.5M CI jobs/year. Decades of A/B testing and feature flags bloated the codebase, pushing developer toil above 90%.

sections.title: Sourcegraph's Mission and Product Line
sections.summary: Beyang explains Sourcegraph's mission to make building software at scale tractable, describing products: code search, large-scale refactoring/migration tools, Cody (context-aware AI coding assistant), and now agents to automate SDLC toil.

sections.title: Booking.com's Cody Adoption Timeline
sections.summary: Bruno traces the adoption journey: Sourcegraph Search deployed ~2 years prior; Cody experimentation began in January with all 3,000 developers, initially limited to one LLM. Multi-LLM access was enabled because different LLMs had different expertise. July brought developer training, converting skeptics into daily users. October brought new KPIs. November results showed daily Cody users 30%+ faster, shipping 30% more MRs. An API layer enabled Slack/Jira integration.

sections.title: KPIs and Measurement Framework
sections.summary: Bruno details four KPIs defined in October with a one-year measurement horizon: lead time for change, quality, coding sites, and codebase modernization. The ultimate goal is compressing codebase replatforming from years to months.

sections.title: From Coding Assistant to Agents
sections.summary: Beyang notes engineers using Cody began composing API calls into longer chain automations—proto-agents. Sourcegraph and Booking.com decided to collaborate directly, flying to Amsterdam for a joint hackathon to build agent capabilities together.

sections.title: GraphQL Schema Search Agent
sections.summary: The first hackathon output was a GraphQL generation agent. Booking.com's GraphQL API is over 1 million tokens—too large for any LLM context window, and naive approaches produced garbage and hallucinations. The agent searches the schema, finds relevant nodes agenticly, walks up the tree to pull parent nodes, and shows its reasoning via inner dialogue before generating a response.

sections.title: Automated Code Migration Agent
sections.summary: The second agent targets automated code migration of legacy functions with 10,000+ lines to accelerate replatforming. Using code search, structured meta-prompts, and divide-and-conquer, the agent identified call sites within two days of the hackathon—work that had previously taken developers months. Bruno emphasizes the value of pairing with experts and the importance of developer education.

sections.title: Customizable Code Review Agent
sections.summary: The third agent targets code review. Beyang notes off-the-shelf AI code review tools lack customization for organization-specific rules. Their agent consumes rules defined in a flat file format, applies relevant ones to modified files in PRs, and selectively posts comments optimized for precision over recall to avoid noise.

sections.title: Future Vision: Declarative Rules and Self-Healing Services
sections.summary: Bruno envisions declaring service rules, shifting CI errors left into the IDE with suggested fixes, and enabling self-healing services by end of year. Beyang connects this to the Mythical Man Month: successful software accumulates tech debt and loses cohesion. Declarative rule enforcement lets senior engineers and architects define constraints that hold across the codebase, enforced at review time and in the editor.

sections.title: Education as the Key Takeaway
sections.summary: Both speakers emphasize education as the single most important takeaway. Handholding entire business units through two-day workshops and hackathons transformed skeptics into passionate daily users who defended the 30%+ speed gains. Bruno invites attendees to visit the Sourcegraph booth and attend his expo talk on agent implementation details.
